elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(i) permits Sparkling to assign the Agreement, without Garman's consent, to any of its affiliates.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor by merger.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(i) permits assignment without consent to a successor by way of merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor by acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(i) permits assignment without consent to a successor by way of acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor through a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(i) permits assignment without consent to a successor through a sale of all or substantially all of Sparkling's assets or business.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence of Section 20(d) requires the other party's written consent for an assignment, so Garman requires Sparkling's written consent.

elements.element: Customer consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) states that required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(ii) expressly provides that Garman may not assign the Agreement to any competitor of Sparkling.

elements.element: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a termination right.
elements.evidence: The final sentence expressly states that no change of control of Sparkling gives Garman any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(i) permits Sparkling to assign without Garman's consent to successors arising through merger, amalgamation, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d)(i) makes Sparkling's permitted successor assignment subject to written notice to Garman.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: No successor carve-out is provided for Garman; all Garman assignments remain subject to Sparkling's written consent.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The written-notice language applies only to Sparkling's assignments. There is no notice-based successor-assignment mechanism for Garman.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments are permitted with Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence permits assignments with the other party's written consent, subject to Sparkling's specific affiliate and successor carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor consent to Customer assignments other than successor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard applies to Garman's consent under the mutual opening sentence.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than successor assignments are permitted with Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Although the general rule permits assignment with consent, Section 20(d)(ii) absolutely prohibits assignments by Garman to Sparkling competitors even if Sparkling would consent. Thus consent is not a sufficient route for every other Vendor assignment.

elements.element: Customer consent to Vendor assignments other than successor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments subject to the consent mechanism, the opening sentence states that Sparkling's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; competitor assignments are separately prohibited.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred position, but not the fallback because Garman receives no notice-only successor-assignment right. The redline is not minimal: it adds a Customer notice obligation, an unreasonable-delay standard, partial-assignment language, and change-of-control protections against suspension and repricing beyond the requested termination protection. It also adds Section 20(d) as an exception to all remaining Section 3(c) restrictions on transferring, leasing, exporting, or sublicensing the Work. Because Section 20(d) addresses assignment of the Agreement rather than those separate acts, that cross-reference is ambiguous and may inadvertently broaden unrelated rights concerning the Work.
